description: Global Mangrove Watch contains global maps of mangrove extent and change; the v4.1 time series released in July 2026 gives annual extent from 1985 built from the full Landsat and Sentinel-2 archives and JAXA L-band radar, using baselines every five years, classifiers run in Google Earth Engine and a Markov chain to enforce plausible transitions. It is produced by a partnership led by Aberystwyth University (P. Bunting and colleagues) with soloEO, Wetlands International, JAXA and others, to support mangrove conservation, restoration and blue carbon policy. Coverage is global tropical and subtropical coastlines; the reported global F1 score is 0.93 from 32,569 reference points. Layers are downloadable from Zenodo as compressed GeoPackage vectors per year and raster stacks, and statistics and further layers such as blue carbon and restoration potential are available on the web portal. The licence is CC BY 4.0, free of charge. Caveats: imagery is sparse before 1999-2000, so earlier years include infilling from other years, and accuracy varies locally. It serves coastal nature-based protection, storm surge exposure and adaptation planning for coastal infrastructure; related records are the Allen Coral Atlas, WDPA, GLWD and the Demak Building with Nature case study.
